cliopatria.citation: Bennett et al. (2025), Cliopatria, Scientific Data 12:247, DOI 10.1038/s41597-025-04516-9. Dated -278 inclusive subset; selected components/relabeling noted.
cliopatria.title: Bennett et al.: Cliopatria, historical political boundaries dataset

dei-factions.role: Reference roster/regional associations only; no copied artwork, game geometry or code.

rome2-factions.role: Official faction families and presentation reference; 272 BCE is not our date.

attalus-278.role: 278 BCE chronology with ancient source references.
attalus-278.title: Attalus: 278 BCE chronology and ancient references

oxford-galatia.role: 278 BCE crossing and later territorial settlement; guards against anachronistic fixed Galatia.
oxford-galatia.title: Oxford Classical Dictionary: Galatia

imperator-reference.role: Faction granularity/presentation reference; 304 BCE is not copied as 278 BCE.

numidia.role: Numidian regional identities; exact 278 extent remains a scenario abstraction.

iranica-bactria.role: Bactria/Parthia secession is later than this scenario; no independent kingdoms invented.
iranica-bactria.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Bactria in the Pre-Islamic Period

terrain-border-review.role: Physical terrain and existing GSHHG WDBII river corridors guide bounded provisional-border drawing. Later ancient associations inform only broad placement; no claim of surveyed or confirmed 278 BCE borders.

polybius-1.role: Later ancient testimony, 1.7-8: Mamertines, Messana and the Campanian garrison at Rhegion; not a contemporary border survey.
polybius-1.title: Polybius, Histories, Book I

polybius-2.role: Later ancient testimony, 2.41: re-formation of the Achaean League and subsequent accession of Aegium.
polybius-2.title: Polybius, Histories, Book II

spring-sicily.role: Later ancient fragments, 22.7-10: changing Sicilian regimes and Pyrrhus' intervention. Akragas-Syracuse is the explicitly approved gameplay aggregation.
spring-sicily.title: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, Book XXII fragments

athens-kallias.role: Inscription of 270/269 recalling earlier events. Civic Athens and Macedonian military positions are distinct; exact Piraeus chronology is qualified.
athens-kallias.title: Athenian decree honouring Kallias of Sphettos, IG II? 1, 911

memnon.role: Later ancient account preserved in an epitome: distinct Bosporus communities, Bithynian politics and Galatian movements.
memnon.title: Memnon, History of Heraclea: surviving epitome

spring-convention.role: Modern concordance to ancient sources. Spring pre-expedition timing is an approved scenario convention, not a claim of an exact day.

iranica-colchis.role: Modern scholarly regional geography; distinguish western Colchis from eastern Iberia.
iranica-colchis.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Colchis

iranica-yuezhi.role: Modern scholarship places the migration into Bactria in the second century BCE. Existing western starting ownership is withdrawn, not the faction identity.
iranica-yuezhi.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Khalchayan and the later Yuezhi setting

strabo-gaul.role: Later testimony for regional associations. Transfers in Gaul are bounded gameplay reconstructions, not verified 278 BCE frontiers.

samarobriva.role: Modern scholarly gazetteer: Samarobriva Ambianorum. The existing Belgae faction is the approved broader regional approximation.
samarobriva.title: Oxford Coin Hoards of the Roman Empire: Samarobriva place record

livy-neapolis.role: Later ancient testimony, Livy 8.26.6-7: Neapolis' treaty relationship. Roman colour represents an allied sphere, not uniform direct administration.
livy-neapolis.title: Livy, History of Rome 8.26?27: Neapolis and the Roman treaty

tacitus-germania.title: Tacitus, Germania

irish-archaeology.title: Heritage Ireland: Mesolithic–Iron Age
irish-archaeology.evidence: Modern archaeological interpretation, Irish Office of Public Works. Does not establish an island-wide state.

iranica-massagetae.title: Rüdiger Schmitt, Massagetae, Encyclopaedia Iranica

dadan-lihyan.evidence: Archaeological regional context around Dadan; precise dynastic chronology remains qualified.
